summary: Forest Service fire tower on Carr Mountain, Wentworth NH, under construction in 1939 and staffed in 1940; four cement footings remain on the summit.

facts.status_note: Four large cement fire tower footings remain on the summit, per NH Family Hikes; the FFLA list shows the tower as gone.

access.note: Trailhead and parking area on Stinson Lake Road in Ellsworth; the summit is in Wentworth. Landowner status not checked.

visit.trail_note: Hiking trail from the Stinson Lake Road trailhead, per NH Family Hikes. No tower to climb.

events.note: Forest Service crew building the tower, expected to be finished within weeks (Portsmouth Herald, August 1939). NH Family Hikes gives 1929 as the start of a tower on the summit.
A worker returned to his job at the Carr Mountain tower (Groton Times, October 1940)
End of the 1929 to 1948 fire tower span given by NH Family Hikes; the page does not say how the tower ended

evidence.supports: Tower being finished on Carr Mountain in Wentworth in 1939
evidence.quote: Towers that will be completed within a few weeks are located on Carr Mountain, elevation 3,470 feet, in northeast section of Wentworth.

evidence.supports: Forest Service crew led by Everett Kimball of Lacinia
evidence.quote: The tower is being built by a Forest Service crew in charge of Everett Kimball of Lacinia.

evidence.supports: 1940 worker returned to his job at the Carr Mountain tower in October
evidence.quote: Malcomb MacKenzie, an appendicitis victim, has returned to his job at the Carr Mt. tower.

evidence.supports: Summit held a fire tower from 1929 to 1948, per the hike guide
evidence.quote: which was home to a fire tower from 1929 to 1948.

evidence.supports: Four large cement footings remain on the summit
evidence.quote: among the four large cement fire tower footings

evidence.supports: Trailhead and parking on Stinson Lake Road in Ellsworth
evidence.quote: Trailhead and parking area are on Stinson Lake Road in Ellsworth, NH

evidence.supports: Views blocked by trees; mountain dropped from the list in 2001
evidence.quote: taken off the list in 2001 because tree growth had obstructed the once panoramic view from the summit.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the tower as gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1939 newspaper item has the tower being finished that year, while NH Family Hikes says a fire tower stood on the summit from 1929 to 1948. The story shows both and does not pick one.
The FFLA list shows the tower as gone, while NH Family Hikes describes footings still on the summit. Status is ruins, since the footings remain.

notes_for_editor: The 1939 and 1940 facts come from a newspaper and a 1940 item, both quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not read. NH Family Hikes gives a 1929 to 1948 span that conflicts with the 1939 construction report; the story keeps both and says the start is uncertain. The footings description is from the hike guide, which is undated, so the 'today' statement rests on that page alone. Access is a trailhead description, not a landowner statement. The Hike Over the Hill list shows 'No Longer Standing / Artifacts' and is not used. The NHDFL state history PDF returned 403, so it is not used.
